reference_sql:
SELECT store_code, country_code,
       COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY country_code) AS country_stores
FROM stores
alternatives:
WITH country_counts AS (  -- one row per country
  SELECT country_code, COUNT(*) AS n_stores
  FROM stores
  GROUP BY country_code
)
SELECT s.store_code, s.country_code, cc.n_stores AS country_stores
FROM stores s
JOIN country_counts cc ON cc.country_code = s.country_code

SELECT s.store_code, s.country_code,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stores s2 WHERE s2.country_code = s.country_code) AS country_stores
FROM stores s

other_way.sql:
WITH country_counts AS (  -- one row per country
  SELECT country_code, COUNT(*) AS n_stores
  FROM stores
  GROUP BY country_code
)
SELECT s.store_code, s.country_code, cc.n_stores AS country_stores
FROM stores s
JOIN country_counts cc ON cc.country_code = s.country_code
other_way.tradeoff: A per-country count joined back works on any engine, but it takes a second step for one number.
